key_insight: The PEA organic spacer slows degradation and improves resistance to light and heat compared with BA in two-dimensional lead iodide perovskites.
engineering_relevance: Spacer selection can improve perovskite durability, but long-term device stability also requires defect control, surface passivation, and encapsulation.
method: Compare BA₂PbI₄ and PEA₂PbI₄ nanoflakes under ambient light and thermal stress.
Probe degradation using confocal micro-Raman spectroscopy.
Analyze chemical changes using X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy.
evidence_signal: Fresh nanoflakes showed comparable room-temperature luminescence, while PEA improved crystal morphology and suppressed lattice defects; both materials degraded through organic-component loss and decomposition into PbI₂ and metallic Pb.
watch_item: The abstract reports no quantitative stability gains or device-efficiency results, so photovoltaic lifetime and performance trade-offs remain unestablished.
paper_title: Impact of organic spacer cations on the light and thermal stability of two-dimensional lead halide perovskites
